text:
maria: FYI saw a ~20% spike in GPU node evictions in us-west1 between 02:10-02:18 UTC. Pods failed scheduling or got evicted; autoscaler spun up spot nodes and they were gone within minutes. Pretty classic eviction wave. We need a detector + hot-standby strategy before the next morning traffic spike.

raj: can you paste the autoscaler events and a short metric window?

maria: pasted a quick PromQL snapshot and the autoscaler events. PromQL: `sum(increase(node_evictions_total[8m])) by (zone)` -> us-west1: 18, others <2. Autoscaler events: `ClusterAutoscaler: scale-up: 6 nodes (gpu-spot-pool) -> started; NodePreempted` repeated 3x.

k8s-bot: [autoscaler] 1987654340: event: ScaleUp: group=gpu-spot-pool size=6 reason=unschedulable-pods; 1987654364: event: NodePreempted: instanceId=gpu-spot-xx; 1987654371: event: ScaleDownAbort: recent evictions.

oliver: two quick notes: 1) i've seen SNAT exhaustion in the same region before; if nodes can't talk to control plane they look unhealthy and get cordoned/evicted — check NAT metrics. 2) an eviction wave across multiple AZs usually means the cloud provider reclaimed a whole subset of spot instances (instance-family or capacity-pool).

maria: good call. i checked NAT ephemeral-pool usage: `gcp_vpc_nat_total_allocated_ips` jumped by 35% at 02:12. control-plane connection errors (5xx kubelet -> apiserver) spiked for ~3m in same window. possible compound failure: network churn + provider-initiated preemptions.

leo: long-term: diversify spot instance families and spread nodepools across more AZs. short-term: we need an automated response — detect an eviction pattern and pre-warm a hot-standby nodepool (on-demand or committed) to absorb traffic.

anya: proposal sketch:
1) eviction-pattern-detector: Cloud Monitoring / Prometheus alert if `sum(increase(node_evictions_total[5m])) by (region) > 10` OR `sum(rate(kubelet_container_restart_count[3m])) > threshold`
2) On alert fire a runbook and trigger an autoscaler override job that scales `gpu-standby-pool` to N nodes and removes the NoSchedule taint for incoming pods (or sets tolerations for emergency).
3) fallback routing: temporarily route new latency-critical traffic to a small fleet of non-GPU inference nodes (quantized models) until GPU capacity stabilizes.

raj: that seems reasonable. concrete implementation options:
- GKE: use Instance Group Manager resize + GKE nodepool patch to change taints.
- AWS: ASG.setDesiredCapacity + node-label/taint toggles via kube-api.
- We can implement detector in Prometheus Alertmanager -> webhook -> autoscaler-lambda (or cloud function).

maria: example playbook command snippets i tested locally:
```
# scale standby nodepool (gke example)
gcloud container node-pools update gpu-standby --cluster=redwood-prod --num-nodes=6 --zone=us-west1-a
# cordon old failed nodes
kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=gpu-spot-pool | xargs -I{} kubectl cordon {}
# toggle standby taint
kubectl taint nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=gpu-standby standby=true:NoSchedule-
```

oliver: also add a short cooldown/confirmation step in the detector: only scale standby if evictions sustained for >5m AND evictions are cross-AZ, otherwise we risk flipping for noisy single-node flaps.

maria: agreed. detection logic:
- condition A (ephemeral): sum(increase(node_evictions_total[5m])) by (region) >= 8
- condition B (persistence): increase(node_evictions_total[15m]) > 0 AND avg(kubelet_heartbeat_failures[5m]) > 0.01
if A && B -> scale standby to min(10, ceil(current_spot_fleet_size * 0.15))

raj: cost note: keeping standby on-demand/committed is ~12-18% overhead vs purely spot, but rolling it as cold standby (only up during events) is cheaper. we should run a short cost sim.

anya: added a quick runbook snippet to the message thread with playbook steps and required IAM roles for Cloud Function to call GCP/ASG APIs. will add to runbook doc.

k8s-bot: [monitoring] created alert `EvictionWaveDetector-us-west1` -> webhook -> /ops/eviction-handler (1987654475)

leo: action items:
- raj: build the detector webhook + autoscaler-lambda (ETA: tomorrow EOD)
- oliver: prepare gpu-standby nodepool template (taints, labels, autoscaling knobs) + validation canary (ETA: 48h)
- anya: update runbook + add test in chaos-canary pipeline to simulate eviction wave (ETA: 72h)
- maria: validate dashboard and update oncall playbook (ETA: today)

maria: one more thing — we should add a dispatcher that changes PodTopologySpread preferences for scheduling to avoid hot-packing on a single AZ during recovery. small change but reduces risk of another correlated eviction wipeout.

raj: noted. will add to PR for kube-scheduler patches.

oliver: thanks all. i'll run a dry-run next low-traffic window and post results here. :thumbsup: :eyes:

maria: thanks folks. adding this to the incident runbook as "eviction-wave + hot-standby". ping me if you need quotas increased for the standby pool.
